candidates.next_evidence: Check latest 10-K for partner concentration, revenue-share formulas, online versus residential enrollment mix, marketing cost intensity, ED/state litigation, and whether partner contract modifications pressure take rate or improve durability.
candidates.node_relation: Direct university services and online program enablement provider; provides services to university partners and has explicit revenue-per-student and revenue-share exposure.
candidates.theme_relation: A public analog to OPM-like enablement for accredited university programs, with direct exposure to online student enrollment, partner university economics, marketing/support infrastructure, and contract terms.
candidates.why_include: Grand Canyon Education reported 2025 service revenue from university partners and disclosed contract modifications involving reduced revenue-share percentages, making it one of the most direct public companies tied to the economics of online degree enablement.

candidates.next_evidence: Verify degree-program revenue contribution, partner retention, revenue-share or fee model, enterprise versus consumer mix, AI product adoption, learner acquisition cost, and whether university degree growth offsets pressure in open courses/certificates.
candidates.node_relation: Direct platform for university-created online degrees, credentials, and courses; more modular and platform-like than traditional full-service revenue-share OPM.
candidates.theme_relation: Potential beneficiary if universities shift away from high-cost legacy OPM contracts toward lower-cost online degree distribution, credential stacking, AI-enabled course support, and modular student-success infrastructure.
candidates.why_include: Coursera’s annual report describes a catalog that includes fully online degrees and university-issued credentials from partners. Its sub-$1B market cap is a limitation, but its strategic relevance to modular online degree distribution is unusually high for this node.

candidates.next_evidence: Track US Higher Education enrollment, persistence, Title IV dependence, gainful-employment or debt-to-earnings exposure, marketing efficiency, employer partnerships, and whether Capella/Strayer outcomes support premium economics.
candidates.node_relation: Direct asset owner and operator of accredited higher-education institutions including Strayer University and Capella University, with shared services spanning IT, financial aid, marketing, legal, HR, and other functions.
candidates.theme_relation: Represents the asset-owner side of the accredited online degree node: owns/serves universities rather than selling OPM services to third-party institutions.
candidates.why_include: Strategic Education’s SEC filing states it has shared-services agreements with Capella and Strayer, including finance, legal, HR, IT, financial aid, and marketing. Capella is an online-focused institution, making STRA a direct public exposure to accredited online degree operations.

candidates.next_evidence: Review enrollment by institution, online degree penetration, clinical-placement constraints, accreditation status, professional licensure pass rates, federal aid exposure, Grad PLUS/federal loan rule sensitivity, and employer partnership durability.
candidates.node_relation: Direct asset owner of accredited higher-education institutions, including Walden University and Chamberlain University, with online healthcare and professional degree exposure.

candidates.why_include: Adtalem’s filings and investor materials identify Chamberlain and Walden as major accredited education assets, with Walden competing in fully online higher education and Chamberlain offering large healthcare degree programs. Healthcare workforce shortages make this a differentiated online-degree exposure.

candidates.next_evidence: Check latest 10-K for institution-level enrollment, retention, graduate outcomes, Title IV revenue concentration, advertising spend, legal/regulatory contingencies, and whether online program economics are improving without quality deterioration.
candidates.node_relation: Direct operator of accredited postsecondary institutions offering online, campus-based, and hybrid programs.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Postsecondary education / online and hybrid universities

evidence.claim: GAO reported that at least 550 colleges worked with an online program manager to support at least 2,900 education programs as of July 2021, and noted many OPMs are paid through tuition revenue-share arrangements that require safeguards against prohibited incentive compensation.
evidence.source_title: Higher Education: Education Needs to Strengthen Its Approach to Monitoring Colleges' Arrangements with Online Program Managers

evidence.claim: 2U, formerly a public OPM leader, emerged from Chapter 11 in September 2024 as a private company after restructuring, making its case a warning signal for legacy OPM economics rather than a current public equity candidate.

The Department of Education released OPM guidance in January 2025 focused on misrepresentation risks, including statements about OPM-run programs being equivalent to campus-run programs absent specific evidence of parity.
evidence.source_title: Education Department releases new OPM guidance

evidence.claim: Grand Canyon Education reported 2025 service revenue of $1.1061 billion, university partner enrollments of 136,239, and disclosed contract modifications with some university partners in which its revenue-share percentage was reduced.
evidence.source_title: Grand Canyon Education, Inc. Reports Fourth Quarter 2025 Results

evidence.claim: Coursera’s 2025 annual report states that partners have created thousands of catalog offerings on its platform, including university degrees, and references more than 50 degrees available through the platform.

Strategic Education’s 2025 Form 10-K states it has shared-services agreements with Capella University and Strayer University covering services including finance, legal, HR, IT, financial aid, and marketing.

Adtalem’s 2025 annual report identifies Adtalem as the parent of Chamberlain University and Walden University and states that the market for fully online higher education, in which Walden competes, remains competitive and growing.
Perdoceo stated that its accredited academic institutions offer postsecondary education through fully online, campus-based, and hybrid learning programs.
evidence.source_title: Perdoceo Education Corporation Reports Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2025 Results

memory_update.text: LOPE is the cleanest public services-provider exposure to accredited online degree enablement because it reports university partner service revenue, partner enrollments, and revenue-share contract changes.
COUR should remain in the universe despite a sub-$1B market cap because it is a direct modular university-degree platform candidate and may fit the shift away from legacy full-service OPM economics.

STRA, ATGE, and PRDO are better classified as accredited online degree asset owners/direct customers rather than OPM suppliers; they provide direct exposure to online degree demand but carry federal aid, accreditation, and outcomes risks.

2U should be tracked as formerly public and now private after Chapter 11; its restructuring is a negative model signal for high-debt, high-revenue-share OPM economics, not proof that all online degree demand is weak.

Need a separate pass for private OPMs, university LMS vendors, CRM/student-success software suppliers, and nonprofit university customers because this Layer 1B pass was constrained to direct public companies and obvious leaders.

node: Accredited online degree enablement and online program management
summary: Expanded universe for the accredited online degree enablement / OPM node. The clearest US-listed exposures are not legacy 2U-style pure-play revenue-share OPMs, because 2U is now private after Chapter 11. Public exposure is concentrated in: platform OPM-like degree marketplaces, university service providers, and asset-owner operators of accredited online universities. The node remains investable-research relevant, but regulatory scrutiny, revenue-share economics, student outcomes, federal aid dependence, and marketing efficiency are primary falsification variables.
